one_liner: Zig CLI that indexes and extracts uncompressed FASTA; builds samtools-compatible .fai indexes 6-21x faster than samtools faidx.
what_it_does: One static executable with four commands for uncompressed FASTA: `index` (default binary `.zfi` index with side tables for ragged layouts, or `--emit-fai` to print a samtools-compatible five-column `.fai` to stdout for uniformly wrapped files), `get` (positional regions, names files and BED intervals with strand, reverse and complement transforms), `validate` (structural, alphabet and header checks, with repair to a separate file) and `stats`. It replaces `samtools faidx ref.fa` and `samtools faidx ref.fa region` for plain FASTA, but with its own command syntax, and it is CLI-only: embedding it from Zig or C is still an open request (issues #35 and #36).
how_it_is_fast: The indexer is single-threaded and streams 256 KiB read() buffers; once a record's first line fixes the line width, it accepts blocks of up to 256 lines at a time by checking the separator bytes at the expected stride and counting bytes at or below ASCII space with portable Zig @Vector code, and drops back to a general line state machine at the first anomaly. HTSlib's fai_build_core, behind samtools faidx, walks the file one character at a time through bgzf_getc, so the gap is per-byte work, not threads or compiler flags. For GET, the binary `.zfi` loads in milliseconds, while samtools takes about 0.3 s per call on GENCODE transcripts whatever the region count, consistent with parsing its text `.fai`, and names are scanned and de-duplicated with 16-byte vector compares and a hash set.
when_to_use: Pipelines that build or rebuild `.fai` indexes of large uncompressed references: human GRCh38 in 0.38 s vs 8.16 s for samtools faidx (warm cache), with byte-identical `.fai` output on the 20 samtools parity cases.

One-shot command-line extraction from FASTA files with many records (transcriptomes, proteomes), where samtools spends most of its time loading the `.fai`: one 1 kbp region from GENCODE transcripts in 8.2 ms with `.zfi` vs 301.8 ms.
BED batch extraction: 10,000 1 kbp rows from the transcriptome in 37 ms vs 377 ms for samtools and 771 ms for bedtools getfasta.
Messy FASTA exports (mixed line widths, trailing whitespace, mixed CRLF/LF, blank lines) that samtools faidx refuses; the `.zfi` side tables index them.
Memory-constrained hosts: indexing stayed near 3.6 MiB peak RSS from 1 MiB to 2.9 GiB inputs.
when_not_to_use: bgzip- or gzip-compressed FASTA, or FASTQ: not supported, so samtools faidx with BGZF remains the tool there.
Inside a C, C++ or Zig program: there is no library API yet, and HTSlib's fai_load plus faidx_fetch_seq pays the index load once per process, which the per-invocation GET benchmark does not measure.
Native Windows: no release; the author points Windows users to the Linux build under WSL.
Cold-cache or disk-bound indexing: every published number is warm page cache (7.9 GiB/s on the genome); cold runs were not measured.

Workflows that need many positional regions in one call (capped at 1,024 per invocation; use a BED or names file instead) or that cannot tolerate a young single-maintainer tool (9 stars, 0.3.x releases since July 2026).

integration.form: CLI executable (static binary, about 800 KiB); no library API
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; building from source needs only Zig
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.16.0 (build.zig.zon minimum_zig_version); build.zig rejects ReleaseSmall, use -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS, x86_64 and arm64 release archives; Windows only through WSL
integration.thread_safety: not applicable (CLI); the indexer is single-threaded
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — `z-fasta index --emit-fai ref.fa > ref.fa.fai` produces the same `.fai` bytes as samtools faidx for samtools-representable FASTA and `get` covers region and BED extraction, but the commands and flags differ, `.fai` goes to stdout only, and BGZF or gzip input is refused

gotchas: Version 0.3.4 indexed records with a space or tab inside a later sequence line as fixed-width, giving wrong lengths in both `.zfi` and `.fai` and returning the whitespace bytes from GET; 0.3.5 fixed it, the stale-index check (sidecar mtime plus source size and mtime, not a content hash) does not detect such sidecars, so re-index those files. The fix made indexing 10-40% slower on 15 of 30 cases (open issue #34); the README numbers are from 0.3.5, after the fix.

Harness: the `--emit-fai` lane writes the `.fai` rows to a spool file in TMPDIR and then to /dev/null while samtools writes a sidecar next to the FASTA (a small difference); samtools 1.24 is a default `./configure && make` build (-O2, shared HTSlib, C compiler unnamed) against a z-fasta built for the host CPU; both sides are single-threaded and warm-cache. No correctness defect found behind the 0.3.5 index numbers: the SIMD fast path still checks every byte for whitespace.

The genome GET gap is a near-constant 5-6 ms from 1 to 100 regions (2.3-2.7 ms vs 7.9-8.6 ms for samtools), and samtools stays near 0.30 s on the transcriptome from 1 to 1,000 regions, consistent with loading its text `.fai`; the GET ratios therefore measure process startup and index loading, not extraction speed.

Index and GET treat every byte above ASCII space as a sequence symbol (alphabet checks happen only in `validate`), duplicate names keep the first occurrence by default, and the `rust-bio` peer lane is a custom FAI writer, not a rust-bio command. The stats report's only C program is seqtk comp (15.50 s vs 2.84 s on the genome), which it labels a partial reference whose output is not the same report.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: needletail is the catalogued sibling for streaming FASTA/FASTQ parsing (including gzip) and beats kseq.h; pick z-fasta instead when you need an index and random access to regions of uncompressed FASTA, or a `.fai` built quickly. The other string-and-text siblings (csv-zero, Sassy, A*PA2) solve different problems.
verified_claims_summary: On an AMD Ryzen 9 3950X (Linux, warm page cache, zebrac 0.6.2 with 5 samples after 3 warmups), z-fasta 0.3.5 (Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseFast, host CPU) built the `.fai` for the GRCh38 primary assembly in 0.382 s vs 8.161 s for samtools faidx 1.24 with HTSlib 1.24 (default -O2 build), 21.3x, plus 11.1x on GENCODE v46 transcripts and 5.8x on the UniProt human proteome, both tools single-threaded. One 1 kbp GET took 2.3 vs 8.2 ms on the genome and 8.2 vs 301.8 ms on the transcriptome, timings dominated by process startup and index loading.
status_note: Active single-maintainer project (244 commits, releases v0.3.0 to v0.3.5 from July to 2026-10-10, 9 stars, 13 open issues) under MIT with prebuilt Linux and macOS binaries; usable as a CLI today, but it has no library API, and 0.3.5 carries an open indexing slowdown (#34) left by the whitespace correctness fix.
